fields.quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant
fields.note: Each element of the requirement appears in the guide's Security Deposits section: the 1.5x cap, pet and prepaid rent counting toward it, the 2.5x inception limit, the 10% yearly increase cap, trust and interest-bearing account rules, notice and 7% remedy, the 30-day, 5-business-day and 15-business-day return deadlines, double damages with costs and fees, and new-owner responsibility.

fields.quoted_span: may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit
fields.note: The 1.5x cap, 2.5x inception total, 30-day return and double damages for wrongful withholding are all stated in the document.
The field is empty and the guide gives no effective date for the law.

fields.quoted_span: The Security Deposit Law applies to most  residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
fields.note: The guide describes the law in the present tense as currently operative. No repeal or sunset is mentioned.

fields.quoted_span: The exception is an owner-occupied two-, or three-family dwelling.
fields.note: The document also supports the 30-day written-request opt-in by the tenant, and the 125-consecutive-day seasonal rental carve-out from the account provisions. It covers mobile homes.
The guide cites this section for the 1.5x maximum deposit. The aliases (46:8-19, -19.1, -21, -21.1, -21.4, -21.5, -25, -26) also appear in the security deposit discussion.
